title.value: Exponential Objective Decrease in Convex Setup is Possible! Gradient Descent Method Variants under $(L_0,L_1)$-Smoothness

abstract.value:
The gradient descent (GD) method -- is a fundamental and likely the most popular optimization algorithm in machine learning (ML), with a history traced back to a paper in 1847 (Cauchy, 1847). It was studied under various assumptions, including so-called $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness, which received noticeable attention in the ML community recently. In this paper, we provide a refined convergence analysis of gradient descent and its variants, assuming generalized smoothness. In particular, we show that $(L_0,L_1)$-GD has the following behavior in the _convex setup_: as long as $||
abla f(x^k)|| \geq  rac{L_0}{L_1}$ the algorithm shows _exponential objective decrease_, and when $||
abla f(x^k)|| <  rac{L_0}{L_1}$ is satisfied, $(L_0,L_1)$-GD has standard sublinear rate. Moreover, we also show that this behavior is common for its variants with different types of oracle: _Normalized Gradient Descent_ as well as _Clipped Gradient Descent_ (the case when the full gradient $
abla f(x)$ is available); _Random Coordinate Descent_ (when the gradient component $
abla_{i} f(x)$ is available); _Random Coordinate Descent with Order Oracle_ (when only $	ext{sign} [f(y) - f(x)]$ is available). In addition, we also extend our analysis of $(L_0,L_1)$-GD to the strongly convex case. We explicitly confirm our theoretical results through numerical experiments.
